label: Out-of-Office Nominee Embraces Prohibition
detail: The party out of the presidency since 1921 nominates a man who pledges to keep the national ban on alcohol and reverses its repeal stance.
assumption: The Democratic nominee personally pledges to keep national Prohibition, and the party platform drops repeal; wet voters and urban immigrants may defect or stay home, while dry voters, especially in the South and rural areas, are reassured.
facts_text: The party out of the presidency since 1921 has dropped its call for repeal of the Eighteenth Amendment in its platform.
Many newspapers report that both major parties now favor keeping the national ban on alcohol.
nominee_news: He announced that, if elected, he would stand behind the national ban on alcohol and oppose repeal of the Eighteenth Amendment.
Editors who favored repeal have criticized him for abandoning the call to end the ban.

add_planks.text: Keep the Eighteenth Amendment in force and oppose its repeal.

research_questions: How did wet urban and immigrant voters respond when a party they favored abandoned repeal?
How did dry Protestant and rural Southern voters vote when both major parties backed Prohibition?
How many voters in 1932 ranked Prohibition above the economy in choosing a candidate?
source_text: fdr adopts a policy to reinstate the prohibition on alcohol
